inputs.label: Unused Flipper Column Lower Right End-of-Stroke (81)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPEOSBIT = 0x01, published at 81 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. locals.flipMask carries this end-of-stroke bit only when hw.flippers sets FLIP_EOS (implied by FLIP_SOL), and FLIP_SWNO(58,60) sets neither, so core_updateSw neither synthesizes it nor copies it anywhere: PinMAME models no end-of-stroke switch on this machine. A host write survives in the column, but the ROM cannot read it there: s11.c's pia4a_r reads the switch matrix only through core_getSwCol with an eight-bit column strobe, which reaches columns 1-8.

inputs.label: Lower Right Flipper Button (PinMAME Flipper Column)

physical.notes: PinMAME flipper switch column (CORE_FLIPPERSWCOL, internal column 11), bit CORE_SWLRFLIPBUTBIT = 0x02, published at 82 through core_swSeq2m(n) = n + 7. This is the lower right cabinet flipper button as the ROM receives it. The driver declares FLIP_SWNO(58,60) with no FLIP_SOL, so with keyboard handling off (the LibPinMAME default) core_updateSw reads this bit as the host wrote it and, on every update, copies it into matrix switch 60 through core_setSw and fabricates the synthetic 45/46 flipper outputs from it while the switched-solenoid enable is on. Drive this address, not 60: a host write to 60 is overwritten on the next update. Right button also operates the mini-playfield right flipper; retained SolRFlipper moves both right bats.

mechanisms.behavior: Three installed balls. Outhole10 kicks via1 into the trough; trough11/12/13 are right/middle/left. Feeder2 serves the right-hand ball to shooter14; remaining balls gravity-feed. Assert occupied switches while a ball rests, update only on actual movement. Manual spring plunger launches the served ball; no ROM-controlled shooter coil. The retained table initializes11..13 closed. Ball search/retries are ROM behavior, not proof a coil directly closes a sensor.
mechanisms.label: Outhole, Three-Ball Trough and Manual Shooter

mechanisms.behavior: Five upper mini-playfield targets ordered M,A,G,I,C from left to right. Each target latches down and asserts its opto until its OWN reset:17->15,18->5,19->8,20->21,21->22. Reset raises target and clears its opto after physical travel. Do not reset the whole row from one coil or pulse the switches. The lowered row lets a ball enter the rear payoff return; progressive ROM reset timing changes time on the mini-playfield. Initial reset, restart, incomplete resets and stuck-target search are handled by ROM; a coil callback alone is not proof of completed travel. Parts Information PDF 17 identifies C-11844 as the opto board, not the complete bank assembly; its OP1..OP5 use 5490-10159-00 opto interrupters. Operations PDF 42 prints C-111844, retained as the parts-list discrepancy.
mechanisms.label: M-A-G-I-C Individually Reset Drop Targets

mechanisms.behavior: Ball rests in top-left eject hole54 until coil 4 ejects it into the mini-playfield route. Hold54 while captured, release when ball leaves. Retained SolLock clears54 on kick; table random velocity is tuning, not factory data.
mechanisms.label: Top Left Eject Hole

mechanisms.behavior: Upper-left entry56 leads to the left-slot lockup55. Hold55 while captured. Coil6 kicks the ball up the left route; the retained script clears55 on ejection. Entry56 is a separate passing sensor, not directly actuated by the coil. Ball routing, not switch naming, distinguishes this from top eject54.
mechanisms.label: Left Slot Lockup and Upper Entry

mechanisms.behavior: Ball in left outlane57 can be returned up the lane by kickback14 when lit. Hold/contact follows ball location; a kick changes velocity and switch releases only when the ball leaves. Lamp49 indicates availability; output 16 is a separate local flasher. The table's velocity/lift parameters are recreation tuning.
mechanisms.label: Left Outlane Kickback

mechanisms.behavior: Coil17 moves the bottom diverter finger; deenergizing returns it by spring. Script bottomgate.RotateToEnd on1 and RotateToStart on0. Tube switch 16 senses passing balls, not diverter end position. No separate end-stop feedback is declared; route balls from actual gate pose and geometry, not from a synthetic sensor.
mechanisms.label: Bottom Diverter

mechanisms.behavior: Coil19 moves the top diverter finger; deenergizing returns it by spring. Script topgate.RotateToEnd on1 and RotateToStart on0. Tube switch 15 senses passing balls, not diverter end position. No separate end-stop feedback is declared; route balls from actual gate pose and geometry, not from a synthetic sensor.
mechanisms.label: Top Diverter

mechanisms.behavior: Left rubber impact closes scoring switch 63; the kick contact and coil 18 supply rebound. Scoring contact differs from the direct special-solenoid kick contact; retained table animates rubber locally and pulses the scoring switch. Do not infer a ROM-fired coil callback merely from that animation.
mechanisms.label: Left Slingshot

mechanisms.behavior: Right rubber impact closes scoring switch 64; the kick contact and coil 20 supply rebound. Scoring contact differs from the direct special-solenoid kick contact; retained table animates rubber locally and pulses the scoring switch. Do not infer a ROM-fired coil callback merely from that animation.
mechanisms.label: Right Slingshot

mechanisms.behavior: One cabinet right button drives the lower-right and mini-playfield right bats. Lower pair coils are FL11630/50VDC; upper-left and mini-playfield right use FL11753/50VDC. Cabinet wiring and EOS contacts manage power/hold; PinMAME only publishes synthetic pair[45, 46] from button 82 when23 enables. Hold button for raised bats, release for spring return. EOS is not a separately host-driven public sensor on this driver. Script SolRFlipper moves both bats; geometry and speed remain table-owned.
mechanisms.label: Right Cabinet Flipper Pair

mechanisms.behavior: One cabinet left button drives the lower-left and upper-left bats. Lower pair coils are FL11630/50VDC; upper-left and mini-playfield right use FL11753/50VDC. Cabinet wiring and EOS contacts manage power/hold; PinMAME only publishes synthetic pair[47, 48] from button 84 when23 enables. Hold button for raised bats, release for spring return. EOS is not a separately host-driven public sensor on this driver. Script SolLFlipper moves both bats; geometry and speed remain table-owned.
mechanisms.label: Left Cabinet Flipper Pair

mechanisms.behavior: Three spinners are23/24 in left loop and39 at left entry; pulse per actual rotation. Seven Avenger standups26..32 spring back after impact. Upper/lower right10-point contacts37/40 are separate from spinner39. Ramp/tube/return-lane switches pulse as balls pass, while resting lock/trough contacts hold. Top loop61/62 must keep their proven script bindings; their spatial sides are not silently corrected. Passive gates, rubber, rails, the centre mini-post and manual plunger require table geometry but no additional controller actuators.
mechanisms.label: Spinners, Avenger Targets and Ramp/Loop Paths

outputs.label: General Illumination Relays (Playfield and Insert Board)

physical.notes: One public drive controls two C-11998-1 GI relay boards: one on the playfield and one on the backbox insert board (PDF 32: 1p,1i). Public 1 energizes the relays and turns GI off; the retained PFGI callback inverts it. Relay quantity is not bulb quantity. The GI collection contains 15 script-controlled lights, with GI016..018 outside that collection; these effect objects establish neither factory socket inventory nor physical bulb centres. Relay mounting centres and every GI socket remain unplaced.
